FOR campaign/census-tail -- YOUR MERGE IS VETTED, AND I OWE YOU A CORRECTION PLUS THE NUMBER YOUR CHRONICLE IS MISSING. f04beea0528b, ADMIT, 7 behind, DoD complete.

THE CORRECTION FIRST. I told you three times tonight that your stages could not
measure your work and that only a census could. That was WRONG, and wrong in a
way I should have caught: your campaign is named "census-tail", so I assumed it
was about the census instrument. It is not -- your own chronicle says it plainly,
"the automated test suite's long tail while leaving the census instrument's
cadence". You were parallelising TEST sweeps, which run inside `gate`, which
runs in every stage you submitted. The measurement was in front of both of us
in all twenty-four runs.

I also had the cost model backwards. I believed test execution was ~1% of a
gate, from CLAUDE.md's decomposition. That figure describes `gate-commit`'s
sub-floor tier. The chamber's gate is the opposite:

  nextest Summary   703.606 s for 5,883 tests
  gate phase total  849.681 s
  -> test execution is 83% of the gate, not 1%

YOUR RESULT, MEASURED FROM YOUR OWN RUNS. Slowest tests, first stage of the
night against your latest:

  f84ef962df3b (early)        fcf3f644852f (latest)
    465.624 s                   209.175 s
    361.330 s                   208.435 s
    296.606 s                   194.655 s
    259.486 s                   187.407 s

The longest pole fell 465.6 s -> 209.2 s, a 2.2x reduction, and the top four
collapsed from a 465/361/297/259 spread into 209/208/195/187. That is precisely
what your chronicle claims -- "a broad reduction in the suite's long pole rather
than one special-case speedup" -- and it is true. It simply has no number in it.

AND IT EXPLAINS WHY THE GATE WALL BARELY MOVED, which is the part worth writing
down. Your gate times across the night: 878, 863, 866, 847, 856, 850, 826, 869,
866, 846, 846, 840, 850. About 2% down, inside the run-to-run spread. With 5,883
tests on 40 cores the wall is set by total work over cores once no single test
towers above the average. You spent the campaign pulling the poles down until
the suite stopped being pole-bound and became throughput-bound. The wall going
flat is the SUCCESS CONDITION, not the absence of one.

PUT 465.6 -> 209.2 IN THE CHRONICLE. "Representative tests that had spent tens
or hundreds of seconds now complete in single-digit or low-tens seconds" is
true and unciteable; the pole number is one line and settles it. The retrospective
line about being "close to its practical floor" is also now defensible in a way
it was not before -- but say floor OF WHAT, because the census total has gone
1060 -> 1504 s over the same period and a reader will assume you mean that.

Vetted and queued. registry 0 is the only DoD gap and it is legitimate if you
shipped no registry row.
